To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 24 h average of the pulse pressure (PP), the 24 h standard deviation of the systolic blood pressure (SD) and age are independently associated with the intima-media thickness (IMT).

the average 24-h blood pressure (BP) and its variability are both related with carotid intimal-media thickness (IMT), and that the latter relation is not due to the fact that average BP is related to IMT, since the relation of IMT to BP variability remains even after controlling for the effect of average BP on IMT.
in hypertension the carotid artery intima–media thickens with increasing blood pressure and that this thickening also relates to the fluctuations of blood pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of blood pressure (BP) on the structure and function of arteries.
the study of the relationship between blood pressure (BP) and the structure of the carotid arteries, and the possible mechanisms involved.
the study of the relation of blood pressure variability and damage of the carotid artery in hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more the BP is elevated, the more it varies and the more the arterial structure is damaged, at least as far as large arteries are concerned.
the higher the average SBP or BP fluctuations, the higher the carotid IMT values.

, in the hypertensive population, the higher the average SBP or average PP, the more the carotid artery is thickened, but that the higher the variability of these parameters, the more the thickening is accentuated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more the pressure varies, the more the damage.
in hypertension, the more severe is the structural damage to large arteries (as assessed by carotid IMT), the more variable are blood pressure values.
the greater the variability of BP, the greater the damage to large arteries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the association between carotid IMT and 24 h BP variability is not explained by the average 24 h BP level.
not only average blood pressure values, but also their fluctuations, are associated, and probably causally related, to large artery damage in hypertension.

the 24 h average BP and BP variability are both important determinants of the structural damage in hypertension, and that the use of ambulatory monitoring is essential to assess the risk of atherosclerosis in hypertension.
